findings.issue: Unpackaged YAML ceiling moved 448→433 (shrink-only), not raised. Packaging entire infra/gitops + infra/talos trees pulled 15 files into the corpus graph (indexed 5351→5366; packages 32→34 / indexed 14→16). This is the intended northstar direction of corpus-index-coverage.

findings.issue: Chesterton: OWNERS + unpackaged ceiling exist as independent fail-closed ratchets, not bureaucracy. OWNERS/reachability close ADR-0555 unowned/unreachable/unjustified; packaging closes corpus_index_unpackaged_regression. Raising the ceiling alone would have greenwashed debt; this PR correctly packages then re-anchors measured ceilings downward.
findings.evidence: G039 diagnosis: firewall FAIL codes unjustified/unowned/unreachable on the two new YAMLs; buck2 corpus_index_unpackaged_regression 450>448. Fix surface: infra/{gitops,talos}/{OWNERS,BUCK}, specs/reachability-registry.json exact prefixes, policy re-anchor 448→433.

findings.issue: Systems second-order: bootstrap-sync already declares an Argo Application (oya.io/cell=local, targetRevision=dev, automated prune/selfHeal) that includes local-path-storage.yaml. Landing the missing manifest on dev completes a latent auto-reconcile path for any local cell that already applied bootstrap-sync — not a warm CAS/RE activation, but real cluster mutation of privileged local-path storage on those cells.
findings.evidence: infra/gitops/bootstrap-sync.yaml lines 27-52 (Application local-path-storage, automated sync, CreateNamespace). Comments restrict to local/dev cells; production called out as CSI. Acceptable residual for isolated proof-cell prerequisites tracked by #1534; not a merge blocker given intentional wire-up and cell label boundary.

findings.issue: Contrarian: packaging only the two new files would have unblocked CI with smaller blast radius; packaging whole trees expands corpus extraction fan-in and review ownership surface. Systems counter: sibling YAML was already unpackaged debt; whole-tree packages permanently shrink the ceiling and prevent the next file in those directories from re-tripping the ratchet. Nested infra/talos/local/patches retains its own BUCK/OWNERS (parent comment + tree evidence), so double-package ownership is not introduced.
findings.evidence: infra/gitops/BUCK and infra/talos/BUCK use corpus_yaml_facts_shards(glob **/*.{yaml,yml}); tree shows infra/talos/local/patches/{BUCK,OWNERS}. Measured package/file deltas match +2 packages / +15 files.

findings.issue: OWNERS for both infra/gitops and infra/talos set to cloud-ci-platform (matches infra/arc and local/patches). Contrarian risk: future non-CI infrastructure changes under those trees route through the CI-platform ownership cell. Acceptable given current platform ownership of proof-cell substrate; not a correctness defect.
findings.evidence: infra/gitops/OWNERS and infra/talos/OWNERS content: cloud-ci-platform; sibling infra/arc/OWNERS and infra/talos/local/patches/OWNERS same token on PR head.

findings.issue: local-path-storage Namespace enforces PSA privileged; ClusterRole can create/delete PVs; helper setup uses mkdir -m 0777 and teardown rm -rf. This is inherent to hostPath local-path provisioner on Talos (/opt RO → /var/mnt/local-path). Mitigations present: digest-pinned images, non-root provisioner container, seccomp RuntimeDefault, drop ALL caps, readiness/liveness, WaitForFirstConsumer.
findings.evidence: infra/gitops/local-path-storage.yaml; structural lock in infra/arc/tests/ci_workspace_capacity.rs cas_proof_cell_has_minimal_network_and_storage_prerequisites; bootstrap-sync comments document PSA + Talos path rationale.

findings.issue: Product YAML and governance packaging/ceiling re-anchor landed in one PR (two commits). Contrarian separation would have left product unmergeable under fail-closed gates. Systems: coupling is required, not optional — gates treat registration and corpus ceilings as merge authority.
findings.evidence: Commits 9bd2fad9 (product) + 86edf077 (OWNERS/BUCK/registry/ceiling); prior red run 30977703798 on product-only head.

findings.issue: No CAS writer/reader activation, ARC credentials, or RE authority in this diff. Reachability-registry anchors explicitly deny live apply authority for BUCK markers and YAML prefixes. Safety boundary holds for the admitted change set.

findings.issue: Buck test locks structural invariants (image digests, PSA label, path map, bootstrap include, cilium patch keys) but does not re-run kubeconform/server-side dry-run inside the gate. Manual verification claimed in PR body; residual is process depth, not a demonstrated product defect.
findings.evidence: infra/arc/tests/ci_workspace_capacity.rs new test; PR verification list includes kubeconform + SSA dry-run + talos config validation as operator evidence, not hermetic buck targets.

summary: Critic B (contrarian + systems_thinking): APPROVE. Exact-head oya-ci-required green on 86edf077; G039 unowned/unreachable/unjustified + unpackaged-ceiling failures fixed by OWNERS+BUCK packaging, reachability exact prefixes, and shrink-only ceiling re-anchor 448→433 (15 files into graph). Chesterton holds: ceilings and OWNERS are fail-closed debt ratchets, not noise. Residual low risks are local-cell Argo auto-reconcile of pre-wired local-path once on dev, privileged hostPath surface, and whole-tree ownership fan-in — all acceptable for isolated proof-cell prerequisites, not high/critical blockers. No warm CAS/RE/credential activation. Not a G039 product-complete claim.
